definition: A technique that simulates a larger effective batch size by accumulating gradients across multiple smaller forward/backward passes before performing a single weight update.
details: Gradient accumulation allows training with an effectively larger batch size than would otherwise fit in available memory, by splitting a large batch into smaller micro-batches processed sequentially before updating weights.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. Think of it this way: A technique that simulates a larger effective batch size by accumulating gradients across multiple smaller forward/backward passes before performing a single weight update. And here is the clever part: Gradient accumulation allows training with an effectively larger batch size than would otherwise fit in available memory, by splitting a large batch into smaller micro-batches processed sequentially before updating weights. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. And that is Gradient Accumulation — the quiet loop that turns flailing into skill.
